To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of heterozygozity (LOH) affecting p53, Rbt, and/or mcc was observed in 35% of heterozygote patients with ulcerative colitis-associated dysplasia/carcinoma.
loss of heterozygo-sity affecting the p53 and Rb and mcc/apc genes was observed frequently in colonic dysplasia and carcinoma occurring in the setting or ulcerative colitis.
loss of heterozygozity of the tumor suppressor gene locus p53 was found in 47% of dysplastic and neoplastic lesions of the colon in patients with ulcerative colitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetic changes associated with the development of cancer in the colon.
the development of an in vitro system for the study of the pathogenesis of colon cancer.
the molecular genetic changes that occur in dysplastic ulcerative colitis and in ulcerative colitis associated cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LOH is a common finding in dysplastic lesions, as well as cancerous lesions, of ulcerative colititis.
allelic deletion at the p53, retiblastoma, and mcc/apcc loci occurs in a significant subset of dysplasias in ulcerative colitis and that these deletions may be involved in the pathogenetic process.
the incidence of allelic deletions of p53, mcc/apc, and Rb is not increased in dysplastic lesions of ulcerative colitides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

allelic deletion at p53, Rbs, and/or mcc/APC is involved in the development and/or progression of a subset of colitis-associated dysplasias/carcinomas, and that these losses occur early in the pathogenesis of these neoplasms.
the p53 gene is the most important gene for the progression of ulcerative colonic dysplasia to cancer.
the loss of heterozygositiy of the tumor suppressor loci is more common in left colon and is more likely to occur in patients with dysplasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic changes in ulcerative colitis and sporadic colorectal cancer are very similar.
LOH of tumor suppressor gene regions may be a common feature of dysplasia and carcinoma in ulcerative colitis and may be an important step in the pathogenesis of this disease.
the polymerase chain reactions (PCR) are a very sensitive method for detecting loss of heterozygosities in cancerous and precancerous tissues.
